name: Beaked Blind Snake
habitat: Loose soil, leaf litter, termite mounds and under stones and logs in gardens, farmland, scrub and forest
range: Most of peninsular India, the Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats; also Sri Lanka and Bangladesh
active: Underground; comes up after heavy rain, mostly at night
ids: A glossy, cylindrical, worm-like snake, plain dark brown to blackish above with a paler underside; no neck and no visible pattern.
The head is a blunt snout that looks like a pointed beak from the side, and the eyes are only tiny dark dots under the scales.
A very short tail ends in a tiny spine that it presses into the soil like a lever; the head and tail look alike.
Harmless, though it is often mistaken for an earthworm or killed as a "baby snake".

look.colour: Glossy dark brown to blackish; paler belly
look.head: Blunt head with a beak-like snout and dot-like eyes
look.body: Long, thin, cylindrical and smooth, with a tiny tail spine

fact: Blind snakes eat ants and termites. A female may lay her eggs in an ants' nest, where the workers leave them alone.

name: Large-scaled Shieldtail
habitat: Moist leaf litter and soil in forest, plantations and gardens on laterite plateaus and foothills
range: Northern Western Ghats and the Konkan (Maharashtra, Goa and neighbouring Karnataka and Gujarat)
active: Underground; comes out at night and after rain
ids: A burrowing snake with a stout, cylindrical body, glossy blue-black or dark brown above and bright yellow or orange patches along the sides.
The belly is yellow-orange with dark markings, and the colour reaches up the flanks in irregular blotches.
A tiny head, shaped like a wedge for digging, and no distinct neck; the tail ends bluntly in a rough, shield-like disc, which gives shieldtails their name.
Harmless to humans; usually found on roads and paths after rain.

look.colour: Blue-black or dark brown, with yellow or orange patches
look.pattern: Irregular yellow side blotches and a yellow-orange belly
look.head: Tiny wedge-shaped head with no neck
look.body: Stout, cylindrical and glossy, with a blunt shield-like tail

fact: Shieldtails dig with their pointed snouts and plug their tunnels with the rough disc on the tail, which blocks out predators.

name: Brahminy Blind Snake
habitat: Soil, leaf litter, potted plants, garden compost and ant or termite nests; found everywhere there is loose soil
range: Throughout India, from the plains to the Himalayan foothills, and across the world as a stowaway in plant pots
diet: Termites, ants and their eggs and larvae
active: Underground; comes up at night and after rain
ids: A tiny, shiny, cylindrical, worm-like snake only about as thick as a thick pencil lead, usually dark brown or black (sometimes silvery or pinkish) with a paler belly.
No visible neck; the head and tail are almost the same blunt shape. The eyes are only tiny dark dots under the scales.
A short tail with a tiny spine. It moves like a worm but is a true snake with scales, and flicks its tongue.
Harmless, and the world's most widespread snake.

look.colour: Shiny black, dark brown or silvery-grey
look.head: Blunt, rounded head without a neck, dot-like eyes

fact: Brahminy Blind Snakes are all female and lay unfertilised eggs. A single snake can start a new population, which is why this species has spread almost worldwide in the soil of potted plants.

name: Perrotet's Mountain Snake
habitat: Wet leaf litter, rocks, soil and plantations in the hills (tea, coffee and cardamom estates) at higher elevations
range: Southern Western Ghats of Tamil Nadu and Kerala (endemic)
active: Mostly at night and in wet weather
ids: A small, stout, dark brown or blue-grey snake with a pale belly and fine rows of lighter flecks along the body (a honeycomb-like look).
A short head and a short, blunt tail; smooth, slightly shiny scales.
A secretive snail-eater of the high hills of the southern Western Ghats. Harmless.

look.colour: Dark brown to blue-grey, sometimes with a violet sheen
look.pattern: Fine pale flecks give a honeycomb look
look.head: Small blunt head

name: Elliot's Shieldtail
habitat: Moist soil and leaf litter in dry and moist forest, scrub and farmland, often under stones and logs
range: Peninsular India: Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra
ids: A burrowing, cylindrical snake that is brown, olive or greyish with scales that look glossy and slightly iridescent, and a bright yellow patch at the base of the head or on the tail.
Tiny head with a pointed snout, no visible neck and a blunt, shield-like tail tip.
Harmless; often found on roads or washed out by rain.

look.colour: Olive, brown or grey with a yellow patch
look.pattern: Plain, with yellow marks on the head and tail
look.head: Tiny pointed head, no neck

name: Khaire's Black Shieldtail
habitat: Moist soil and leaf litter in evergreen forest, plantations and gardens in the hills
ids: A shiny blue-black burrowing snake with iridescent scales that gleam blue, green and purple in light; sometimes with a pale stripe along the belly.
A tiny head that continues in a smooth line into the body, and a short, blunt tail ending in a rough disc.
Harmless, and rarely seen outside the rains.

look.colour: Glossy blue-black with an iridescent sheen
look.head: Tiny head without a neck

name: Perrotet's Shieldtail
habitat: Moist soil and leaf litter in high-altitude evergreen forest, shola and plantations
range: Hills of the southern Western Ghats (Tamil Nadu and Kerala)
ids: A burrowing snake that is dark brown, reddish-brown or purplish with a glossy, iridescent sheen and a paler, pinkish-brown belly.
Tiny pointed head with no neck, and a short tail ending in a blunt, scaly disc.
Harmless; seen when ploughing or after heavy rain in the high hills.

name: Wynaad Black Shieldtail
habitat: Moist soil and leaf litter in evergreen forest and plantations in the hills
range: Southern Western Ghats (Wayanad and neighbouring districts of Kerala and Karnataka)
ids: A shiny, cylindrical blue-black to purplish-black burrowing snake with an iridescent sheen, often with a pale or yellowish belly.
A tiny pointed head with no neck and a blunt tail tip.
Harmless.

name: Phipson's Shieldtail
habitat: Moist soil, leaf litter and gardens in forest and on laterite plateaus
ids: A burrowing snake with a dark brown to bluish-black back and a pale yellow or whitish spot at the base of the snout or tail.
Tiny pointed head with no neck; short tail ending in a shield-like disc.
Harmless; found on roads and paths after rain.

name: Madurai Thorntail
habitat: Moist soil, leaf litter and gardens in hill forest
range: Southern Western Ghats of Tamil Nadu and Kerala
ids: A burrowing, cylindrical snake that is brown to reddish-brown or olive with a glossy sheen and a pinkish belly.
Tiny pointed head with no neck; the tail ends in a blunt, spiny disc.
Harmless.

name: Assam Snail-eater
habitat: Hill forest, bamboo and gardens, on shrubs and the ground; hunts snails and slugs at night
range: North-east India (Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Arunachal Pradesh) and eastwards
ids: A slender, laterally flattened snake in brown, orange-brown or yellowish with dark cross-bars or flecks, and a blunt, broad head with large eyes.
A very blunt snout and short lower jaw suited to extracting snails from their shells; no heat pits.
A harmless snail-specialist.

look.colour: Brown to orange-brown, with a yellowish tint
look.head: Blunt broad head with large eyes

name: Little File Snake
habitat: Shallow sea, tidal creeks, mangroves and estuaries; rarely on beaches
range: Coasts of India (Maharashtra, Gujarat, the south-east coast and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands)
ids: A fat-looking, grey-brown snake with loose, baggy skin that hangs in folds, banded with dark and pale cross-bars.
Small, rough, granular scales (like a file) rather than smooth overlapping ones, and tiny eyes and nostrils on top of a flattish head.
Usually found in the sea or in tidal creeks, and helpless on land. Harmless.

look.colour: Grey-brown to blackish with paler bands
look.head: Small flattish head with upturned nostrils
look.body: Baggy loose skin and tiny, granular scales

name: Dussumier's Water Snake
habitat: Ponds, paddy fields, streams and wet ground in lowlands and foothills
range: Kerala and neighbouring parts of the southern Western Ghats
ids: A slim, smooth, shiny snake in dark brown or blue-black with narrow pale stripes along the sides and a pale belly.
A narrow, rounded head and small eyes; spends its life in water or wet ground.
Rear-fanged and mildly venomous, harmless to people.

look.pattern: Narrow pale stripes along the sides
look.head: Small rounded head and small eyes

name: Gerard's Water Snake
habitat: Mangroves, tidal creeks, estuaries and mudflats along the coast
range: West coast of India (Maharashtra, Gujarat), the Sundarbans and east coast, and the Andaman Islands
ids: A stout, grey-brown or olive snake with a pale belly and often a pale stripe along the flank.
A small flattish head with small eyes set high; lives in tidal mud, where it hunts crabs.
Rear-fanged and mildly venomous, harmless to people.

look.pattern: Plain, sometimes with a pale side stripe
look.head: Small flattish head, small eyes
